## What is wrong
Flawed recursive JSON.stringify replacer.

## Evidence
Line 28:
```javascript
  const json = JSON.stringify(data, Object.keys(data).sort());
```

## Inferred reason
Using `Object.keys(data).sort()` as the replacer array causes JSON.stringify to recursively filter all nested objects using that same key whitelist, silently dropping any keys not present in the top-level keys list.

## v26.7.3 gate impact
Deterministically drops nested keys during serialization, generating unstable hashes.

## Required proof to promote
Pass a custom sort serialization implementation or use a stable JSON-stringify package.

## Recommended next action
Implement a custom helper to recursively sort keys before serialization.

## Do not do
- Do not pass a sorted keys array as the replacer parameter of JSON.stringify for deep/nested objects.
